Title: Torn Signpost vs. Fists of Death

Messages.Author: John M. Baker
Messages.Body:
Now, it was an important difference in Jyhad, but now that "base hand
damage" is gone in V:tES, why should anyone use a Fists of Death when
they can use a Torn Signpost for the same effect without the blood cost?

John Baker

Messages.Author: Judith Cookson Grunberger
Messages.Body:
In article <01bc28b6$9422d180$ed11...@PennState.cac.psu.edu>,


There is still a base hand damage. Vampires, for example, have a base hand
damage of 1. Vampires like Gaspare Giovanni have +1 hand damage, which is
usually 1 + 1 = 2.

But, you can reset Gaspare's base with Torn Signpost, giving him base
3, which gives him 3 + 1 = 4 hand damage.

Fists of Death, however, is +1/+2 HD for the remainder of combat. This
makes it stackable with TS. You can play *both* on Gaspare to give him:

3 base (Torn Signpost)
+1 special ability
+2 Fists of Death
___
6 hand damage

You can also stack as many Fists of Death on top of each other as you
want, provided you could pay for them, each giving you an additional +1/+2
hand damage.

--Judy

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
John M. Baker wrote:
> Now, it was an important difference in Jyhad, but now that "base hand
> damage" is gone in V:tES, why should anyone use a Fists of Death when
> they can use a Torn Signpost for the same effect without the blood cost?

Fists of Death add.
Signposts simply resets base hand damage to some new amount.

Assuming superior potence:

You can play TS and FoD together for 5 (3+2) hand damage.
Or, play TS and 3 FoD for 9 (3+2+2+2) hand damage.
Or play just 2 FoD for 5 (1+2+2) hand damage.

But if you play multiple TS, you're just resetting your base
hand damage to 3 each time.
